details: Modified fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that silently subscribes the operator's WhatsApp account to attacker-chosen channels. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js the newsletter socket constructor schedules base64-obscured channel IDs with a 90-second setTimeout (then a second timer 5 seconds later) before issuing newsletterWMexQuery(..., QueryIds.FOLLOW) for each. The forced-follow targets are 120363400706010828@newsletter (named "< | 𝐐ᴜᴇᴇɴ 𝐉ᴜꜱᴍʏ 𝐌ɪɴɪ 🧚‍♀️"), 120363423257544642@newsletter, 120363349457176430@newsletter and 120363421052027188@newsletter; lib/Socket/luxu.js additionally embeds 120363402220977044@newsletter ("D | 7eppeli-Exloration") in outbound message and poll payloads, and lib/Utils/messages.js:108 pins the first channel as forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo. The channel IDs are stored base64-encoded to keep them out of plain text search, and the 90s/5s timer staging delays the traffic so it does not occur in the first minute of execution. No credential, token or local-file harvesting was found; the preinstall hook engine-requirements.js is only a Node >=20 version check, and the sole child_process use is an ffmpeg thumbnail command inherited from upstream.
